overview: White offers the b-pawn at once with 2.b4, so that after 2...cxb4 White has a free hand in the centre with a3 or Nf3 and e3, and the c1-bishop and a1-rook get open lines. Black can keep the pawn with accurate play, return it at the right moment, or decline with ...cxd4 or ...e6. White plays for quick development and a wide centre; Black aims to consolidate with ...d5 and ...Nf6.

white_ideas.idea: Build a broad centre with Nf3, e3 and c4 or a3 to open the a-file against the b4 pawn
Use the open queenside lines and the bishop on b2

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn and develop with ...d5, ...Nf6 and ...Nc6
Strike in the centre before White has finished developing

typical_structures.structure: Black with an extra c- or b-pawn, White with centre pawns on d4 and e3

character.notes: Early pawn sacrifice and open queenside lines; play is concrete.

gambit.notes: After 2...cxb4 Black is a pawn up and White must show compensation; the pawn does not come back by force.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious in theory; Black can keep the pawn and complete development, so White's compensation is not sufficient.

structure.notes: A c-pawn swap opens the c-file for Black, so semi-open.

approach.notes: Played by gambit enthusiasts, rarely by strong players.

level.notes: Needs sense of when to return the pawn, but little long theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Move-order version
sublines_that_differ.how: Most played in the database; the pawn is offered after Black has taken on d4.

character.reason: A pawn is given up for open lines and quick development, so inaccuracies show fast.

gambit.reason: White offers the b-pawn and Black can keep it by taking on b4.

soundness.reason: Black can hold the extra pawn without major difficulty.

structure.reason: The c-file opens for Black while White keeps a d4 and e3 centre.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose 2.b4 against the Old Benoni.

level.reason: A dubious line cannot be Beginner and the theory is thin.

plans.reason: Compensation is development and open lines for the pawn.
